item.title: Ackland F.A.M. Day: "Care and Concern" and "Continental Shift" — Sun Sep 27, 2:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
Join us for family-friendly fun at Ackland F.A.M. Day, this Sunday, September 27, 2026! F.A.M. (Families at the Museum) Day is a free, drop-in program for all ages. Drop-in any time between 2-4 p.m. to make art inspired by the works in Care and Concern and take your creations home with you. Explore art throughout the Museum with Ackland Bingo, coloring pages, and journaling activities. item.title: Building Our Brains: From RNA Biology to Evolution — Tue Sep 29, 12:30 PM — Nanaline Duke 147
item.description:
Debby Silver is a Duke School of Medicine Distinguished Professor of Neuroscience and Professor of Cell Biology, Molecular Genetics and Microbiology and Neurobiology. Her lab investigates cell biological and genetic mechanisms governing cerebral cortex development and contributing to neurodevelopmental pathologies and cortical evolution. They use fixed and live imaging, genomics, organoids, and mouse models to understand post-transcriptional control of neurogenesis, as well as human-specific features of brain development.
Source: Duke University

item.title: The Gift of a Corpse: Ordinary Necropolitics in Contemporary Singapore — Tue Sep 29, 3:00 PM — Friedl 225
item.description:
Anthropologist and mortician, Ruth E. Toulson, takes you behind the scenes in a Singaporean funeral parlor.
While multiple authors have probed the corpse's power as a potent political symbol, much of the existing literature on necropolitics has an exclusive focus on contexts of violent regime change, on the bodies of political leaders, or of "the dead" understood as an undifferentiated mass.
In Singapore, in contrast, Toulson argues that the manipulation of corpses is a quotidian strategy of political power, part of the everyday actions of a stable state. What's more, the corpses this state puts to its use are those of ordinary people, whose unremarkable deaths are marked in what seem initially to be unremarkable ways.
The embalmed body, she argues, is a particularly fraught sites of the politic. But how this comes to be is a puzzle, for the state has little interest in legislating ritual or grief. Toulson offers a new anthropology of death, one both more personal and politicized, a

item.description: 5 Points Gallery is proud to present Durham Sweet Durham, a new exhibition of oil paintings by Featured Artist Jim McKeon celebrating the vibrant soul of the Bull City through crisp realism and touches of fantasy. From historic brick warehouses to the wild banks of the Eno River, familiar Durham landscapes become evocative scenes of memory, community, and place. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our ten Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. item.description:
Come connect with us over a run! Hosted by Latinos Run and Latinas Run of Raleigh & Durham, all paces and people are welcome weekly starting at 6:30pm. We’ll follow a 3–4 mile route through downtown Durham before returning to us here at Glass Jug Downtown for drinks and camaraderie. Latinos Run and Latinas Run are nationwide running organizations dedicated to empowering and connecting communities through running, wellness, and culture. Their mission is to create a supportive, inclusive space where individuals of all backgrounds and fitness levels feel welcomed and encouraged to move their bodies and build meaningful connections. item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Dec 26, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Healing Histories: A Trauma-Informed Approach to Confronting the Legacy of Racial Covenants — Tue Sep 29, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
Throughout the 20th century, communities in many parts of the United States used racial covenants to codify neighborhood segregation, a structural legacy that continues to drive inequities in health and economic success today. In this Think Global panel, experts with backgrounds in history, education and social justice will explore how communities are confronting the ongoing impacts of this often-hidden history, a process that can be a powerful tool in building stronger communities that are better able to flourish and respond to adversity.
Panelists will describe the community engagement process of Mapping Prejudice, an internationally recognized research project that works with communities across the United States to mobilize volunteers to identify and map racial covenants. The discussion will explore how this process has created collective understanding and led to policy change in places such as Minneapolis, and how a trauma-informed approach is essential to empowering communities.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Dec 25 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

item.description: The pace of production for new and existing synthetic chemicals is continually increasing, rapidly outpacing our capacity to assess risks of exposure to these substances. Here I will discuss my research group's work towards answering the question: How does molecular structure impact a chemical's potential to accumulate in the body, and how can we use this knowledge to prioritize chemicals of concern during nontarget analysis (NTA)? item.title: Navigating Challenging Personalities — Mon Sep 28, 12:30 PM — None
item.description:
For employees of Duke University and DUHS Continuing Education Credits (CEUs): 0.4
In every workplace, you're likely to encounter some challenging personalities. The first step in dealing with a possible conflict situation is to determine if and how you might be contributing to the situation. This course will identify four types of conflict, how to defuse emotionally charged situations, and how to identify and deal with negative behaviors.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Participatory Deportation Defense: Becoming Abogades de Confianza — Mon Sep 28, 12:30 PM — Perkins Library 218
item.description:
Focusing on the role that deportation defense lawyers play in legitimizing the deportation regime, this talk addresses the responsibilities lawyers have when representing people within an unjust legal system. What does it mean for an immigration lawyer to genuinely earn the trust of undocumented communities and become an abogade de confianza? Borja explores how lawyers can work alongside families, community organizers, and participatory defense campaigns to challenge detention and deportation. So doing, they can help center the leadership of criminalized people by supporting mutual aid efforts, court watch projects, and freedom campaigns. Borja's public talk casts light on what effective immigration advocacy can look like and encourages us to rethink the conventional wisdom that good legal representation alone is enough to produce justice.

item.title: Designing AI-Enabled Workflows — Mon Sep 28, 1:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
Most AI projects don't fail because the technology isn't ready, they fail because the workflow around it was never designed with AI's actual strengths and limitations in mind. This workshop teaches you how to think before you build: how modern AI works at a conceptual level, where it excels, where it predictably breaks, and how it differs from traditional software. You'll learn a practical decision framework for determining whether AI, traditional automation, or a simple process improvement is the right answer for your use case.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Dr. Hortense Spillers Public Lecture — Mon Sep 28, 4:00 PM — East Duke 209
item.description:
Join us on Monday, September 28th at 5:00 PM in East Duke 209 for a public lecture by Dr. Hortense Spillers, a black feminist thinker of unparalleled influence and a foundational figure in African American literary and cultural theory. Reception to follow. RSVP required (please click the "More event information" button to access the RSVP form).
Talk title: Oedipal Deferral: Implications of the Middle Passage
Hortense J. Spillers is Gertrude Conaway Vanderbilt Professor of English, Emerita, at Vanderbilt University. She received her Ph.D. from Brandeis University and has held appointments at Wellesley College, Haverford College, Emory University, and Cornell University. Her visiting positions include Duke University's Program in Literature and the John F. Kennedy Institute for North American Studies at the Free University of Berlin. item.title: Weekday Carillon Recital — Mon Sep 28, 5:00 PM — Duke Chapel
item.description:
Each weekday at 5:00 p.m., a Duke Chapel carillonneur plays a fifteen-minute recital on the bells in the Duke Chapel tower. The recital begins with an opening excerpt of music, then a bell tolls five times to mark the hour, and then the carillonneur plays a selection of hymns and other songs appropriate for the day.
Listen to the recital anywhere outside on West Campus or online via the livestream on the Duke Chapel Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/DukeChapel.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Adobe Acrobat Express for Design and the Ethics of AI — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
For members of Duke's Creator Lab:
Adobe Acrobat Express for Students is Duke's newest Adobe offering, now available to all students. Come get hands-on with the platform and explore how Adobe tools and AI can help you create, communicate and build skills for what's next.
In this 90-minute interactive session, Todd Taylor, Ph.D., pedagogical evangelist at Adobe, will cover Adobe AI, how it compares with other platforms, the ethics of generative AI, building a skills portfolio, and the "habits of mind" that help you ask smarter questions about emerging technologies.
The workshop will be ideal for students who want to improve their digital content production skills, especially for social media.
Bring a fully charged laptop and download Adobe Express, Creative Cloud or any Adobe apps you use before the session so you can jump right in.
Seating is limited. Registration details coming soon.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Duke Arts Create, With Our Hands: Quilting and Community — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — None

Participants will learn the basics of hand sewing while creating an improvised mini quilt using fabric, needle, and thread. No prior sewing or quilting experience is necessary. All materials will be provided, though we encourage participants to bring any small embellishments or sentimental fabric scraps.
